title: Compact KV page reclamation and GPU swap coordinator
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Our current KV cache uses large contiguous slabs and a basic LRU-style eviction that interacts poorly with continuous batching patterns and bursty sequence lengths. This leads to knee-of-load GPU memory pressure and occasional host/GPU swap storms that increase P95/P99 latency for generation requests. Goal: introduce a compact page reclamation mechanism plus a lightweight GPU Swap Coordinator to (1) reduce fragmentation, (2) prefer reclaiming cold micro-pages without stalling active KV lookups, and (3) orchestrate controlled async swap-to-host to avoid swap storms while preserving latency SLOs.

Proposed design: 1) Micro-page format: break existing slabs into 256KB micro-pages (configurable). Each micro-page holds homogeneous KV stripe ranges to allow fine-grained eviction without invalidating large contiguous contexts. 2) Resident-set tracking: maintain a small resident metadata structure in GPU DRAM that summarizes owner model, last-access timestamp (monotonic tick), and batch-hotness score derived from recent continuous-batching access patterns. 3) Compact reclamation pass: run incremental compaction that coalesces partially free micro-pages into contiguous regions during low-SLO windows (background thread pinned to a separate CPU core). The pass avoids copying hot KV entries by only compacting pages with hotness score below threshold. 4) Swap Coordinator: an async orchestrator that schedules GPU->host pinned-memory transfers for eviction candidates. It limits concurrent swap streams, enforces a moving-window rate cap, and prioritizes pages predicted to be cold by an exponential-decay access model. The coordinator exposes backpressure signals to the request router to temporarily throttle non-critical batch merges when swap backlog is high. 5) Prefetch and hinting: integrate with the batching layer to add prefetch hints for expected next-token kv ranges for active sessions (heuristic-based: recent sequence growth + model prefix similarity). Hints are soft and can be dropped if swap budget is exhausted. 6) Fault modes and graceful fallback: the runtime can fall back to a conservative eviction policy (coarse LRU) if the coordinator is overwhelmed or if device temperatures indicate thermal throttling. 7) Telemetry & observability: emit per-page lifecycle events, swap queue depth, swap latency histogram, compaction throughput, and hotness score distributions to the console dashboards.

Engineering trade-offs: - Smaller micro-pages reduce unnecessary data movement but increase metadata overhead (resident-set entries). We propose a tunable micro-page size with default 256KB—empirically a good compromise for common open transformer KV sizes and batch distributions. - Aggressive prefetch reduces misses at the cost of additional memory pressure; the swap coordinator's rate-limiter mitigates this. - Compaction while serving risks CPU/GPU interference; we limit compaction to off-peak CPU cores and throttle kernel launches.

Interactions with continuous batching: The resident-set hotness uses per-batch access telemetry so the comparator can prefer keeping pages that participated in recent high-concurrency batches. Continuous batching will be extended to annotate requests with session-stability signals (short-lived vs long-lived streams) which inform eviction prioritization.

Rollout plan: implement behind runtime feature-flag; stage canary on 10% of Dedicated pools with strict metrics guardrails; expand to 50% if no regression; enable default after two weeks of stable metrics.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RWI/Compact+KV+Reclamation+Design (internal). Implementation PRs will be in github.com/redwood-inference/serving (see comments).
acceptance_criteria: Adds micro-page allocator with tunable page_size config and resident metadata without regressing baseline tests
Swap Coordinator enforces concurrent_swap_streams and rate cap config and exposes metrics (swap_queue_depth, swap_latency_ms)
Under synthetic mixed workload (tokens/sec + varied seq lengths) P95 latency increase <= 5% compared to baseline with equal throughput
OOM incidents reduced by >= 60% in benchmarked overcommit scenario (simulated multi-model co-residency)
Integration tests for compaction correctness (no KV corruption), and soft-fallback path exercised in CI
Console dashboard shows per-page lifecycle events and a new card for swap_backlog and compaction_throughput
